gary_2026_11_12_education_x_ai_futures_w.title: Education x AI Futures Workshop w/ Plan A
gary_2026_11_12_education_x_ai_futures_w.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_11_12_education_x_ai_futures_w.summary: Gary's Guide: Advanced AI is here, & it is up to all of us to take action toward a safe & thriving Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) future. In this interactive session, students, educators, & leaders from the education field spanning generations move through plausible AGI futures. We'll workshop through worst-case scenarios & best-case outcomes for the field of education in the United States-informed by previous expert roundtables & deep research from RAND, Anthropic, the Council on Foreign Relations, & more. We will then translate that insight into action-what education leaders & students can do to both prevent catastrophic outcomes & to design for the best of what AGI could enable: a future where humanity & technology evolve together toward greater human flourishing. Coffee & pastries will be provided. Plan A is mobilizing business & civil society leaders to shape a safe & thriving AI future. Plan A convenes society's leaders through immersive workshops to prepare for AI futures. They work on two fronts: future proofing (planning for the worst cases), & future building (imagining the best cases), by asking what we actually want our future to look like. This work serves public benefit & is philanthropically backed-giving gives them the independence to test different approaches to driving action, building toward impact rather than a predetermined structure. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

gary_2026_11_12_clean_data_salon_clean_d.title: Clean Data Salon - Clean Data, Stronger Business
gary_2026_11_12_clean_data_salon_clean_d.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_11_12_clean_data_salon_clean_d.summary: Gary's Guide: A Clean Data Salon: Clean Data, Stronger Business -- with Clean Data Alliance An evening of practical insights, founder connections, & collaborative problem-solving. Your customer data is your most valuable asset. Join the Clean Data Alliance & New York Tech Alliance at Civic Hall on November 12 to explore how to acquire & maintain clean, protected customer data in order to earn customer trust & support business growth in the age of Ai. Connect with founders, operators, & practitioners for networking & lightning talks followed by an interactive roundtable exercise. What to expect Understand Clean Data: Jay Mandel introduces Clean Data principles & explains how clear choices & trustworthy information can create value for businesses & customers. See a practical application: Walk through how better customer information can improve an offer, communication, or customer experience. Learn from experience: Guest presenters, to be announced, shares an example from their work & lessons attendees can apply. Build something together: Work with a table of eight to develop one to three practical goals around a Clean Data principle. Make useful connections: Meet people working through similar challenges in their startups & organizations. Who should attend: Founders, Entrepreneurs & Business Leaders - Building customer-centric, data-driven organizations. Technology, AI & Data Professionals - Working in data management, AI, cybersecurity, & privacy. Marketing & Customer Experience Leaders - Using customer data to build trust, engagement, & growth. Educators, Researchers & Students - Exploring data ethics, digital literacy, & emerging technologies. Privacy, Consumer Rights & Digital Advocacy Professionals - Championing transparency, responsible data use, & consumer protection. Nonprofit, Government & Policy Leaders - Advancing responsible technology & public trust. Investors, Advisors & Innovation Ecosystem Leaders - Supporting organizations building trustworthy, sustainable businesses. Agenda 6:00-6:25 | Arrival, refreshments, & networking 6:25-6:35 | Welcome & introductions - Jay Mandel, MC, with host remarks 6:35-7:20 | Three presentations - Jay Mandel, Wendy Louise Wilder, & a guest presenter 7:20-7:35 | Audience Q&A moderated by Jay Mandel 7:35-7:45 | Break 7:45-7:50 | Roundtable instructions & commitment example - Jay Mandel 7:50-8:25 | Facilitated table discussions & commitment development 8:25-8:45 | Table reports - guided by Jay Mandel 8:45-8:55 | Combine commitments, identify next steps, & invite adoption 8:55-9:00 | Closing & follow-up

gary_2026_11_12_can_ai_help_nonprofits_f.title: Can AI Help Nonprofits Fundraise?
gary_2026_11_12_can_ai_help_nonprofits_f.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_11_12_can_ai_help_nonprofits_f.summary: Gary's Guide: Doors open at 6 p.m.; programming starts at 6:30 p.m.Giving season means a lot of work for nonprofit teams: writing appeals, reaching donors, processing gifts, & keeping track of it all. Where can AI helpand how do you use it without losing the personal connection that makes people want to give?Join Aboard for a conversation with Allison Fine of Every.org, Dr. John Brothers of Candid, & Jeffrey Klein of The Center about practical ways nonprofits can put AI to work during their busiest fundraising season. Well discuss where to start, what deserves a humans attention, & how to tell whether a new tool is actually helping. Along the way, well consider donor privacy, staff capacity, & how time saved on administrative work could become time spent building relationships.Aboards head of product, Chris Sassine, will introduce the discussion, which will be followed by an audience Q&A. Afterward, stay for food, drinks, & conversation with the speakers & fellow attendees.About the speakers:Allison Fine is president & CEO of Every.org, a nonprofit giving platform that accepts nearly all forms of cash & non-cash assets & is itself a nonprofit. An author & longtime leader at the intersection of technology & social good, she co-wrote The Networked Nonprofit & The Smart Nonprofit: Staying Human-Centered in an Automated World with Beth Kanter.Dr. John Brothers is interim president & CEO of Candid, a nonprofit that connects people working for social good with data, information, & resources. He previously led the T. Rowe Price Foundation & T. Rowe Price Charitable. His career spans community organizing, nonprofit leadership, philanthropy, & teaching management & social policy.Jeffrey Klein is chief operating officer of The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual & Transgender Community Center in New York City. The Center provides recovery & wellness programs, youth support, advocacy, arts & cultural programming, & space for community organizing, connection, & celebration. Jeff brings the perspective of a community-serving nonprofit to a discussion about what it takes to introduce new tools while keeping an organizations people & mission at the center of its work.

gary_2026_11_14_ai_hackathon_hack_the_un.summary: Gary's Guide: Hack the Unreachable An AI research hackathon powered by Flashpoint.AI People say one thing & do another. Public narratives rarely match private sentiment. The most valuable signals sit with people no survey ever reaches. Spend a day building AI that closes that gap. Use Flashpoint.AI's research platform & Anthropic's models to build agents that uncover what people actually think & turn it into something useful. Tracks Governance: Agents that surface constituent preferences & find policies people can agree on Economic Signals: Hyperlocal sentiment & economic research Self-Improving AI: Models that identify what they don't know & go get it from the right people News & Reporting: Agents that research, verify, & report Investment Alpha: Find the gap between what's priced in & what key segments privately believe Prizes: $800 total 1st Place: $500 2nd Place: $200 3rd Place: $100 What you get Free Anthropic API access for the event Mentorship from the Flashpoint.AI team Judging by Flashpoint.AI, Pioneering Minds AI, & others Lunch provided Who should come Builders, researchers, PMs, designers, & anyone curious about AI. All backgrounds welcome. Come solo or bring a team of up to [4]. Submissions Teams submit a public GitHub repo & share their build on LinkedIn or X. Ship something real, show it off. Come for the networking. Connect with founders, VCs, PMs, & AI practitioners from across NYC right after the hackathon wraps. Arrive by 3:30 PM to watch teams present live & see the winners crowned, then stay to network. Details Saturday, November 14 10:00 am - 6:00 pm Room 333, Gabelli School of Business, Fordham Lincoln Center Hosted by the Fordham AI Society & the Gabelli Product Management Club. Sponsored by Pioneering Minds AI. Spots are limited. Register now.

gary_2026_11_17_wind_win_startup_showdow.summary: Gary's Guide: Step into the Future of Ocean Renewables: An Electrifying Evening with the 2026 Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator Cohort!The 4th annual Wind-Win Startup Showdown offers a pitch experience like no other, spotlighting cutting-edge technology breakthroughs to transform the future of ocean renewables. This is a special year for us: the program set a record high: 118 applications & the strongest competition reviewers have seen to date. In 2026, we also drew in a more diverse cohort than ever before by broadening this year's technology scope a 123% increase in application numbers compared to last year's, reflecting the parallel growth in industry demand for novel solutions needed in the market.Presented by the Offshore Wind Innovation Hub, this networking & pitch event brings together stakeholders across the climate landscapeinvestors, founders, academia, industry, & thought leadersfor an evening of connection, collaboration, & celebration.Come see it for yourself! Join us to engage with leading innovators tackling climates most complex challenges with bold, next-generation solutions.Refreshments & light hors d'oeuvres will be provided.AgendaDoors OpenKeynote + Welcome RemarksAlso on stage: Tone Sndergaard, Director, Offshore Wind Innovation Hub at NYU Tandon Urban Future LabInnovator Lightning Pitches by the 2026 CohortEach of our Offshore Wind Innovation Hub partners has sent their most experienced innovation experts to provide feedback for each of the selected cohort companies.Sam Jung, SVP, Green Economy, New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC)Lyndie Hice-Dunton, Executive Director, National Offshore Wind Research & Development Consortium (NOWRDC)Robert Fenton, Head of Americas Generation Procurement, rstedStephan Kremers, Senior Technical Project Manager, VestasFireside Chat on Dual-Use Technology AdaptationNetworking & RefreshmentsMeet our 2026 FinalistsBlue Ocean Transfers Group (BOT) (New York, US) - Multipurpose, hybrid electric support vessel enabling maritime decarbonization.Bubble Robotics (California, US) - Resident fleet of autonomous underwater robots monitoring offshore infrastructure.Clema (New York, US) - Thermoelectric cooling vest for workers in extreme heat.Fleet Robotics (Massachusetts, US) - Data insights powered by submersible, autonomous cleaning & inspection robots.Hefring Marine (Iceland) - Intelligence platform combining onboard hardware with software to optimize marine operations.HiFIT USA (New York, US) - Impact treatment welding to enable life extension & lighter structures.NeuralX (California, US) - Underwater video & computer vision for fisheries monitoring & ecological data.Sail GTX (New York, US) - Platform for smarter customs workflows for offshore wind components.TMA The Hazardous Goods Companion (Germany) - RFID & AIoT inventory visibility & predictive inventory management solution.Tree Composites (The Netherlands) - Composite joints for offshore support structure to realise material & manufacturing optimization.Vital Ocean (Oregon, US) - Intelligence platform combining ocean data, marine environment, & decision interface.Stay tuned in the next few weeks on our website & LinkedIn for updates on our selected cohort!Innovation in FocusOur 2026 cohort takes the stage to pitch ocean & maritimes most promising technologies. This year's lineup features innovations spanning ports, O&M, environmental monitoring & coexistence, workforce development, installation, construction, & commissioning, maritime applications, among others. The scope doesn't just stop there. The majority of this year's solutions are dual-use, carrying relevance across adjacent industries & global markets, a reflection of just how far the blue economy reaches.Marking the official launch of the 2026 Innovator program, this event offers a unique chance to connect directly with the founders behind these ready-to-scale solutions. Explore their real-world impact, uncover new business opportunities, & spark the kind of strategic partnerships that move ideas forward.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator ProgramA world-class program open to global offshore wind innovators. Building on three successful cohorts, this eight-month intensive program provides unparalleled support for innovators looking to develop novel technology & advance commercialization in New York & beyond.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub is an initiative led by Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering & the National Offshore Wind R&D Consortium (NOWRDC) in collaboration with the New York State Research & Development Authority (NYSERDA) & New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC).The Innovator program is also supported by industry partners Equinor, rsted, & Vestas.

jc_culture_10003578_2026_11_25_hamilton_.label: Festival / Market
jc_culture_10003578_2026_11_25_hamilton_.place: Hamilton Park, 9 McWilliams Pl., Jersey City, NJ
jc_culture_10003578_2026_11_25_hamilton_.summary: Join us at the Hamilton Park Farmers Market, your midweek destination for fresh, local, and thoughtfully crafted food and goods. Each week, we’re proud to feature farm-fresh produce from Stony Hill Farm alongside a curated selection of specialty vendors. Browse a variety of offerings including our long time vendor Pickles and Olives, fresh seafood from Scale Fish Market, and prepared foods perfect for dinner. You can also find baked goods, candles, personal care products, and more. You can even take advantage of convenient services like on-site knife sharpening while you shop. On the first and second Wednesdays of each month, enjoy live entertainment that adds to the vibrant, community atmosphere of the market. Whether you’re shopping for the week, grabbing a bite, or simply enjoying the park, the Hamilton Park Farmers Market is a welcoming space to connect with local vendors and neighbors.
